The main takeaway from our work is that
sex-based disparities in outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarctions (STEMIs) are not explained by differences in the use of evidence-based medical therapies.

the use of a GP IIb/III a inhibitor in patients undergoing PCI is associated with a lower rate of death, myocardial infarct and stroke, as well as a lower rate of repeat revascularisation procedures, compared with the use of aspirin and clopidogrel.

the use of a combination therapy of a glycoprotein II b/IIIa inhibitor and a thrombin inhibitor may be beneficial for patients with STEMI who present with ST-segment elevation and a TIMI 0 or TIMI 1 flow in the infarct-related coronary artery.
